title: Dumbbell Centric Upper/Lower
author: Drew M.
desc: For people with limited equipment to have a balanced and varied program that targets every muscle.

ss.note: Position yourself perpendicular to the bench for the best stretch.
Pick any grip, but then stick to it. Find a ROM that suits your goals, and don’t go weighted until you NEED to.
Form can be awkward on this one. Swap this for a lift that works the side and/or rear delts if you despise this lift. Lu Lateral Raises for example.
Form is key to nail on this one. I recommend recording it and perfecting form over time.
I love to grip dumbbells on the floor for a deeper stretch. Keep a slow eccentric.
Recommend hanging legs off a bench for more stretch. Use ankle weights to up the intensity if you need to, and go slow on the way down.
One arm at a time. Use your incline bench, and select a weight approximately 5-10lbs lighter than standard DB curls.
I recommend using a decline bench. Go painfully slow on the way down.
Do these one leg at a time. Bonus stretch points if you find a structure to hang your heel from. Grip a sturdy place for stability.
Goblet Squats are…decent. Elevate your heels and hold dumbbells to your sides for an improvement.
Place towel on forehead, hang head off a bench, place dumbbell as comfortably as possible on head, and curl with careful form. Sometimes plates work better (if you own them). Don’t go to failure.
I would say the ideal on this one is a neck harness. If not, you could risk lying on a bench and extending neck with a dumbbell held behind head. Swap for Farmer’s carries for more traps if desired.
It may take years to go weighted. Don’t sacrifice form, and earn the weighted pull-ups.
Known as the Barrel Press. I recommend looking into a tutorial.
On this day, do your sit ups with a twist on the way down for obliques work. Decline bench as usual for sit ups to get best stretch.
On this day, do your push ups with your feet elevated on the bench. Slow negative as usual.
Lean against a wall for better stretch.
Everyone prefers a different incline and technique. Find yours. Do lengthened partials at the end if you want to cook your biceps further.
Foot close to the bench, elevated foot directly behind you for quads focus.
Legs close together, dumbbell on top, heels hanging from a platform or structure. If this set up is impossible for you, do them one leg at a time standing, just like on your last leg day.
Grab two dumbbells, hinge back, bend over, and row. Use body english as desired to suit your goals.
There are many ways to do this movement. I recommend keeping your knees off the bench. Find your style, but focus on selecting a swift to maximize the stretch.
We’ve already done these this week, so treat today as a fun day to focus on pumping blood and getting a good stretch. Use a lighter weight than previous day.
Swap for pinwheel curls if you have a strong preference.

If you don’t have rings, pick favorite chest OR shoulder press and swap. Bonus: you can wear socks on a slick floor while gripping dumbbells to slide feet back and forth during push-up to mimic rings.
As always, I recommend a decline bench, and slow negative.
Remember, feet positioning to fit your goals. Planted foot close to the bench equals more quad.
Today it’s time to do these with a twist again. Oblique work.
If you feel stable, grip two dumbbells (straps recommended) and do your calf raises. If not, pick one of the other variations you have in this program that work better for you.
Not to be confused with an RDL, although they can have similar benefits.
Grip onto a stable surface to aid you as you reach failure. Once you can’t do anymore, go into painful negatives and cheat your way to the top.
